skill.name: golang-cli
skill.description: Build, extend, and review Go command-line applications with Cobra and Viper. Covers commands, flags, configuration, output, versioning, signals, completion, exit codes, and tests.
skill.summary: Practical patterns for reliable, scriptable, and testable Go command-line applications.
skill.author: samber

No malicious behavior, prompt injection, data exfiltration, unsafe command execution, or covert system access was found.

content.value_statement: Go command-line projects need consistent commands, configuration, output, shutdown, and testing patterns. This skill applies practical Cobra and Viper guidance with reusable Go examples.
actual_capabilities: Structures Cobra root commands and subcommands with focused files and minimal entry points.
Configures persistent and local flags, argument validation, constraints, and completion suggestions.
Layers flags, environment variables, configuration files, and defaults through Viper.
Separates program output from diagnostics and supports table, plain, and JSON formats.
Implements version metadata, exit-code mapping, graceful signal handling, and shell completion.
Tests Cobra commands programmatically with captured output and table-driven cases.
limitations: Examples are reference patterns and are not a complete, buildable application.
The skill focuses on Cobra and Viper, with limited guidance for other CLI frameworks.
Project-specific business logic, deployment systems, and release pipelines require additional design.
Dependency APIs can change, so current official documentation should confirm signatures.

use_cases.title: Start a Go CLI
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable Cobra command tree with flags, configuration, output rules, and a minimal entry point.
use_cases.target_user: Go developers starting a command-line project

use_cases.title: Extend an Existing Tool
use_cases.description: Add subcommands, configuration sources, shell completion, or machine-readable output while preserving established project structure.

use_cases.title: Review CLI Behavior
use_cases.description: Check exit codes, signal handling, output streams, argument validation, and command tests for predictable automation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Cobra command named [command]. Add [arguments] and [flags]. Keep main minimal and return errors from command handlers.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Go CLI command

prompt_templates.title: Add Layered Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Viper configuration to this CLI. Use prefix [prefix], optional file [path], flag bindings, defaults, and clear precedence.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Automation Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this command for scripting. Separate stdout and stderr, add table and JSON output, define exit codes, and add shell completion.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Long-Running CLI
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this server command for production. Add context cancellation, SIGINT and SIGTERM handling, timed shutdown, typed errors, and command-level tests.

output_examples.input: Design a deploy command with required environment and tag flags.
output: A command layout with declarative argument validation.
Required environment and tag flags with mutual-exclusion rules.
Viper bindings and completion values for supported environments.

output_examples.input: Review a list command that mixes logs with pipeable output.
output_examples.output: A review that moves records to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, and recommends selectable table, plain, and JSON formats.

output_examples.input: Add graceful shutdown to a server subcommand.
output_examples.output: A design using signal-aware context cancellation, SIGINT and SIGTERM support, a shutdown timeout, and distinct handling for normal server closure.

best_practices: Read the existing command tree before changing structure or shared behavior.
Bind configurable flags explicitly and document the precedence of every configuration source.
Test commands through Cobra interfaces so arguments, output, and errors remain observable.
anti_patterns: Do not call process exit functions inside command handlers because deferred cleanup will not run.
Do not write logs or diagnostics to stdout because they corrupt piped output.
Do not require a configuration file when defaults and environment variables can provide valid settings.

faq.question: Which Go CLI libraries does this skill emphasize?
faq.answer: It uses Cobra for commands and flags, plus Viper for layered configuration.

faq.question: Can it help with a standard library flag application?
faq.answer: Yes, but its detailed examples focus on Cobra and Viper. Simple tools may use the standard flag package.

faq.question: Does it provide complete application code?
faq.answer: It provides focused reference examples. You must connect them to your modules, dependencies, and business logic.

faq.question: How does it support shell scripts?
faq.answer: It separates data from diagnostics, recommends stable exit codes, and supports machine-readable output formats.

faq.question: Does it cover shell completion?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Cobra generators for Bash, Zsh, Fish, and PowerShell, plus custom flag and argument suggestions.

faq.question: Can it review an existing CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks command structure, configuration binding, output streams, exit behavior, signal handling, completion, and tests.
